summary: Process switch `mechanical_pass_tier` lets a project run the writer passes of backlog, Operation contract and Solution Design reviews that only apply the fixes a review verdict names on a `mechanical` tier. The default, `role_tier`, keeps today's behaviour. At `mechanical`, such a pass runs on the owning writer's generated `-mechanical` variant and render, stamp and check steps run as direct entry commands with no role pass, while triage, authoring, design, code repairs and every review, re-check and calibration keep their roles and tiers. Every build ships `product-owner-mechanical`, `qa-engineer-mechanical`, `devops-engineer-mechanical` and `solution-architect-mechanical` on a new `mechanical` execution tier (Claude's `strong` model class and Codex's `fast` class, each at effort `high`, starting values that a frozen-task A/B sets before a project opts in). On Codex every variant moves its writer from Sol to Luna; on Claude only `solution-architect-mechanical` runs a lower model, while the other three variants run the writer's Sonnet at effort `high`, lower only when the session runs above `high`, so each host contract states what a variant changes; the writers themselves keep their tier. `tools/validate.py` rejects a mechanical variant for a read-only reviewer or challenger and a switch that declares no writer variants. `templates/task-input-policy.json` declares the pass kinds `apply_findings`, `render`, `stamp` and `check` and the documents each writer's `apply_findings` pass may change. `task_inputs.py --pass-kind apply_findings` binds the verdict's findings, a JSON record whose every finding carries its exact `repair`, narrows the write scope to the owning writer's documents among the inputs, and refuses the kind for a review, re-check, calibration, triage or repair task, for a role the switch declares no variant for, outside the switch's owning flows and at `role_tier`; `render`, `stamp` and `check` derive no role task.
